business_ops.seasonality: The production and sale of technical textiles and consequently sales volumes may be affected by general economic or industry conditions, including seasonal trends in the agriculture sector, recessionary trends in the global and domestic economies and volatility in construction. The cyclical nature of the agriculture and construction industries, both globally and in India, impacts the demand for packaging of bulk commodities, which in turn affects demand for machinery and equipment for manufacturing technical textiles. In particular, the agricultural sector is inherently seasonal and is further impacted by factors including agricultural commodity prices, costs of fertilizers and adverse weather conditions. Similarly, the construction sector is prone to seasonality owing to factors such as the inconsistent real estate market and economic downturns that cease construction activity. No seasonality figures or quarterly split for the issuer's own revenue are disclosed in the routed text.
business_ops.supply_chain_integration: Backward integration capabilities reduce dependence on external supply of parts and components for machine manufacturing and support services and enable maintenance of quality control. The Company designs and manufactures inverters, customized machine controllers and motors along with other products for its circular weaving machine and winders, and operates its own surface mount technology manufacturing line for printed circuit board assembly and testing, so inverters, controllers and motors are made in-house for use either as original parts or spare parts. It has an in-house sheet metal fabrication shop catering to all sheet metal part requirements, 100 computer numerical control (CNC) machines that manufacture parts required in its machines, and a 3D coordinate measuring machine (CMM) from a global internal precision-equipment supplier for adherence to specifications. Electrical parts like inverters and printed circuit boards are also produced in-house using imported electric parts manufacturing equipment, aided by electrical assembly shops at each manufacturing facility where electrical panels are assembled. Other manufacturing steps are integrated through plating shops, moulding shops, assembly and testing shops and paint shops located within the manufacturing facilities, minimising dependence on external service providers. On the inbound side, raw materials, parts and components are sourced from suppliers on a purchase order basis, usually valid for one and two years, without formal long-term agreements; key externally sourced components include extrusion die, pump and screw, gear-box, bearings, electric motors and drives, and certain key components such as electrical motors, sensors, PLC systems, invertors and gear boxes are procured from limited suppliers in India, Europe, USA, China and Japan. Forward reach is through an exclusive global sales network: four sales offices in India (Ahmedabad, Bengaluru, Kolkata, New Delhi) plus a corporate office, five international offices (Brazil, Russia, Thailand, UAE, USA), warehouses in India, UAE and USA, stockists in eight countries, 17 exclusive sales agents, and service engineers stationed in 12 cities in India and in 12 countries overseas.

Key externally sourced components are extrusion die, pump and screw, gear-box, bearings, electric motors and drives. Raw materials are sourced on a purchase order basis (usually valid for one and two years) with no formal long-term supplier agreements; some purchase orders require the Company to obtain insurance on materials supplied, bear freight costs and make 100% upfront payments prior to shipment. internal_operational.detail: The Company owns and operates six machine manufacturing facilities, with four in India and one each in USA and Italy, along with one live experience centre in India. Two Indian facilities are in Kanpur, Uttar Pradesh (with the live experience centre, where flexible intermediate bulk containers are manufactured) and two in Bengaluru, Karnataka; the USA facility is in Burlington, North Carolina and the Italy facility in Como. Warehouses are in India, UAE and USA. Almost all revenue is generated from these facilities, which are subject to operating risks including political instability, strikes and lock-outs, regulatory compliance, scheduled downtimes, equipment breakdown, industrial accidents, power or water disruption, severe weather, natural disasters and outbreak of infectious diseases.

strategy_growth.detail: The Company is among the leading global manufacturers of machinery and equipment for technical textiles by revenue in 2024, with a strong focus on solutions for producing PP and HDPE woven fabric and sacks. A significant portion of revenue from operations is derived from manufacture and supply of machines for woven fabric and sacks. Demand depends on end-use products with packaging and non-packaging applications such as agriculture, horticulture, fisheries and forestry textiles, architectural and constructional textiles, clothing textiles and geotextiles. The agriculture, textiles and construction industries are cyclical and the agricultural sector is inherently seasonal. Changes in government policies, such as amendments to the Jute Packaging Material (Compulsory Use in Packaging Commodities) Act, 1987, may affect demand.
strategy_growth.evidence: "In 2024, we ranked among the top global players by revenue, with a 15.4% share of the global woven Raffia machinery market by value." Revenue from woven raffia machines: Fiscal 2025 Consolidated 12,017.05 (87.28% of revenue from operations); Demerged Business Fiscal 2024 9,989.17 (85.68%); Fiscal 2023 16,753.77 (90.71%). "For instance, in December 2023 and October 2024, the Ministry of Textiles, GoI ordered at least 20% of the total produced sugar to be mandatorily packaged in jute-based material."
strategy_growth.title: RF 3: Heavy dependence on the performance of the woven raffia machines market and its end-use industries

strategy_growth.detail: The global market faces environmental regulations and anti-plastic sentiment, high capital costs for advanced machinery, competition from alternative materials such as biodegradable, paper-based and jute-based packaging, raw material and component price volatility, and skilled labour shortages for machine operation. Within India, specific threats include stringent environmental regulations, rising competition from low-cost importers from China and other Asian suppliers, technology obsolescence and a modernization gap, volatility in raw material costs given reliance on petroleum-based polymers such as polypropylene, and shortage of skilled workforce for digital transition.
strategy_growth.evidence: "Despite being reusable, woven bags are still grouped under broader plastic ban or negative perceptions in many regions." "Indian machinery manufacturers have started facing competition from Chinese and other Asian suppliers offering cheaper machines."
strategy_growth.title: RF 5: Challenges facing the Indian and global woven raffia machines market

strategy_growth.detail: The Company faces significant competition from other woven raffia machine manufacturers. Key players in the global market include Starlinger & Co. GmbH, Yongming Machinery, Hengli Machinery, Tianfeng Plastic Machinery, Polystar and JP Extrusiontech. Sales and business face risks relating to rapid technological change, development of new machinery and their rapid obsolescence, evolving industry standards and significant price erosion or depreciation over the life of the machinery. Competition is primarily on product functionality, quality and reliability; design and technical skill; research and development; production capabilities; ability to meet customers' order requirements and delivery schedules; customer relationships and after-sales services; and product price.
strategy_growth.evidence: "We are a market leader in the domestic woven Raffia machines market, with a dominant market share of 40.7% by value, in Fiscal 2025."

The three-year record is not a like-for-like series: FY2025 is Restated Consolidated, FY2024 is a Restated Standalone shell with nil revenue and PAT of ₹(0.09) million, and FY2024/FY2023 comparatives are voluntary Special Purpose Combined and Carve-Out statements of the Demerged Business; the DRHP itself states neither set "should be used to forecast or accurately predict our future performance with any degree of certainty" (RF 46).

Revenue is concentrated in one machine family: woven Raffia machines were 87.28% of FY2025 revenue from operations (₹12,017.05 million), with circular looms at 31.54% and tape extrusion lines at 17.05% of the product split.

Order book has not grown across the period: ₹8,284.57 million as of March 31, 2025 against ₹7,692.40 million (March 31, 2024) and ₹8,747.62 million (March 31, 2023); the DRHP states order book information is not audited and may not be actualised (RF 17).

Demand history is volatile: carve-out revenue fell from ₹18,470.09 million in FY2023 to ₹11,658.08 million in FY2024 on fewer units produced, change in product mix and decline in sales to Africa, Asia Pacific (ex-India and China), Europe and MENA, before the FY2025 consolidated ₹13,768.72 million (RF 18).

Control remains concentrated after the Offer: Promoters and certain Promoter Group members held 93.00% of the issued and paid-up Equity Share capital as of the DRHP date, with Raj Kumar Lohia alone at 55.47%; the post-Offer promoter percentage is not populated in this draft (RF 51).

Competing-business overhang: Lohia Trade Services Limited (the Demerged Company, a Promoter Group member holding 7.37% and majority owned by Promoters Raj Kumar Lohia and Gaurav Lohia) remains authorised under its memorandum of association to manufacture technical textile machinery, and the non-compete under the September 12, 2022 Family Settlement Agreement runs only for a 10-year Non-Compete Period, after which signatories may commence, acquire or invest in competing businesses (RF 22).

The 'Lohia Group' brand is not owned but licensed to the Company by Lohia Trade Services Limited under a licensing agreement dated July 25, 2024 that is revocable and non-exclusive and terminable by the Demerged Company on a significant breach or a substantial change in the ownership of the Company (RF 31).

Group exposure to loss-making entities: a corporate guarantee of ₹413.00 million was issued on behalf of subsidiary Leesona Corp, USA to HSBC, and Leesona Corp posted a FY2025 loss of ₹102.12 million after a ₹38.26 million profit in FY2024; Lohia Global Solutions FZE lost ₹20.08 million in FY2025; group company Lohia E-Mobility GmbH is under insolvency proceedings expected to complete in 2027 (RF 7).

Overseas revenue of 58.18% in FY2025 sits against a net unhedged foreign currency exposure of ₹(492.00) million (FY2024 ₹(780.00) million, FY2023 ₹(1,536.80) million), with US-dollar revenue at 43.80% and Euro at 10.03% of FY2025 revenue (RF 9).

A show cause notice has been issued to Independent Director Dinesh Kumar Mittal, including for violation of certain provisions of the SCRA, the SEBI Act and the SEBI Listing Regulations; aggregate amount involved in matters against Directors is ₹1.34 million (RF 37).

Inventory quality: a write-down of ₹143.77 million for slow and non-moving inventory was taken in FY2025 on inventories of ₹2,962.12 million, with inventory turnover of 2.59x (FY2024 2.27x, FY2023 3.14x) (RF 33, RF 32).

verdict.our_read: Woven-Raffia machinery maker with 40.7% domestic and 15.4% global share by value and FY2025 revenue of ₹13,768.72 million at 31.71% ROE, whose thesis rides on whether the FY2025 consolidated base is repeatable against carve-out FY2023 revenue of ₹18,470.09 million.

parameter_scores.basis: 40.7% share by value of the domestic woven Raffia machines market in Fiscal 2025 and 15.4% of the global woven Raffia machinery market by value in 2024; installed base of over 2,300 tape extrusion lines, 468,000 winders and 96,000 circular looms as of March 31, 2025.

Three non-comparable bases across the disclosed period: FY2025 Restated Consolidated; FY2024 Restated Standalone with nil revenue and PAT of ₹(0.09) million; FY2024 and FY2023 Special Purpose Combined and Carve-Out statements of the Demerged Business, which the DRHP says involve estimates, assumptions and allocations and are not of the Company as it stands today (RF 46).

ROE 31.71%, ROCE 30.45%, EBITDA ₹2,286.02 million and PAT margin 8.5% on the Restated Consolidated FY2025 basis, against carve-out ROE of 11.92% (FY2024) and 23.66% (FY2023) and PAT margins of 2.54% and 3.06%.

Carve-out revenue ₹18,470.09 million (FY2023) to ₹11,658.08 million (FY2024), then ₹13,768.72 million on the FY2025 consolidated basis; order book ₹8,284.57 million at March 31, 2025 versus ₹8,747.62 million at March 31, 2023, and stated to be unaudited.

Net debt to equity 0.47x at March 31, 2025 versus 1.06x and 1.24x in the two prior years; total borrowings ₹1,851.74 million as of June 30, 2025; CRISIL AA-/Stable (cash credit, term loan) and CRISIL A1+ (forex forward, LC and BG, loan equivalent risk); no covenant default in the last three Fiscals per RF 16.

FY2025 Restated Consolidated CFO of ₹1,412.84 million against PAT of ₹1,178.41 million, with CFI ₹(312.93) million and CFF ₹(877.68) million; carve-out CFO was ₹1,115.14 million in FY2024 and an outflow of ₹(167.87) million in FY2023 (RF 6).

Woven Raffia machines were 87.28% of FY2025 revenue from operations; circular looms 31.54%, other machines and equipment 20.54% and tape extrusion lines 17.05% of the product split; exports 58.18% of revenue with top five export jurisdictions Egypt 4.39%, Iraq 4.21%, USA 3.99%, Sri Lanka 2.82% and Indonesia 2.58%.

Absolute related party transactions were 33.36% of FY2025 revenue from operations (₹4,593.39 million) versus 17.76% and 6.61% in the two prior years; recurring counterparties include United Trade.Net India (₹777.9 lakhs purchases FY2024), Vivsun Engineering (₹367.2 lakhs FY2024) and Sarjna Capfin, from which borrowings of ₹2,474.0 lakhs were taken in FY2024; corporate guarantee of ₹413.00 million for Leesona Corp.

Promoters and certain Promoter Group members hold 93.00% pre-Offer with Raj Kumar Lohia at 55.47%; board of 8 with 4 Independent Directors; show cause notice to Independent Director Dinesh Kumar Mittal under the SCRA, SEBI Act and SEBI Listing Regulations; auditor other matter on internal financial controls of two Indian subsidiaries; Promoters Raj Kumar Lohia and Gaurav Lohia may be entitled to a mutually agreed share of profits on non-machine commercialisation of assigned inventions (RF 53).

234 on-roll R&D employees (13.48% of on-roll manpower as at May 31, 2025) and R&D expenditure of ₹371.13 million (2.70% of FY2025 revenue, against 3.16% and 1.55% in the prior two years); 60 patents granted in India, 28 applied for, 56 granted globally; DSIR-accredited Hargovind Bajaj R&D Centre and NABL-accredited TTRC.

The Offer is entirely an Offer for Sale of up to 42,259,970 Equity Shares of face value ₹1 each and the Company will not receive any proceeds; there is no fresh issue. Offer size, Price Band, P/E and market-cap-to-revenue multiples are shown as placeholders, post-Offer promoter holding and dilution are not quantified, and the promoters' contribution and lock-in table is marked "To be updated in the Prospectus". The only valuation reference disclosed is the peer P/E band of 29.32 to 165.66 with an industry composite of 81.01.

Contingent items as of March 31, 2025: claims not acknowledged as debts ₹46.62 million, GST ₹17.12 million (penalty confirmed by order dated January 31, 2025, under appeal), income tax ₹0.17 million, capital commitments ₹54.23 million and corporate guarantees ₹413.00 million; litigation aggregates of ₹38.84 million by the Company, ₹17.29 million against the Company and ₹1.34 million against Directors; UPSIDA consent for the Offer unanswered and the Bengaluru facility building without an occupancy certificate.

red_flags: Related party transactions equal to 33.36% of FY2025 revenue from operations (₹4,593.39 million), roughly five times the 6.61% ratio of FY2023, alongside promoter-affiliated borrowings from Sarjna Capfin Private Limited (₹2,474.0 lakhs taken and ₹3,847.1 lakhs repaid in FY2024).

A ₹413.00 million corporate guarantee to HSBC on behalf of subsidiary Leesona Corp, USA, which swung from a ₹38.26 million profit in FY2024 to a ₹102.12 million loss in FY2025; group company Lohia E-Mobility GmbH is in insolvency proceedings expected to complete in 2027.

The Promoter-majority Demerged Company, Lohia Trade Services Limited, remains authorised under its memorandum of association to manufacture technical textile machinery, and the family-settlement non-compete is time-limited to a 10-year Non-Compete Period.

The 'Lohia Group' brand under which the business operates is licensed from Lohia Trade Services Limited on a revocable, non-exclusive basis and may be terminated on a substantial change in the ownership of the Company.
A show cause notice has been issued to Independent Director Dinesh Kumar Mittal, including for violation of certain provisions of the SCRA, the SEBI Act and the SEBI Listing Regulations.

The owner of the building housing the Bengaluru manufacturing facility has not obtained an occupancy certificate as required by the local planning authority byelaws, which the DRHP states may compel relocation of that facility; UPSIDA consent for the Offer remains unanswered.
A ₹143.77 million write-down for slow and non-moving inventory was recorded in FY2025 against inventories of ₹2,962.12 million.
strengths_observed: Stated market share of 40.7% by value in the domestic woven Raffia machines market in Fiscal 2025 and 15.4% of the global woven Raffia machinery market by value in 2024 (RF 3, RF 8).
FY2025 Restated Consolidated return ratios of ROE 31.71%, ROCE 30.45% and PAT margin 8.5%, against Demerged-Business carve-out PAT margins of 2.54% (FY2024) and 3.06% (FY2023).

Net debt to equity fell to 0.47x as at March 31, 2025 from 1.06x (FY2024) and 1.24x (FY2023); total borrowings ₹1,851.74 million as of June 30, 2025; CRISIL AA-/Stable on cash credit and term loan and A1+ on short-term facilities.
FY2025 cash conversion: CFO of ₹1,412.84 million against PAT of ₹1,178.41 million, versus a carve-out CFO outflow of ₹(167.87) million in FY2023.
Export share of revenue rose from 35.81% (FY2023) to 49.50% (FY2024) to 58.18% (FY2025), led by MENA (10.03% to 16.62%) and North and South America (4.87% to 12.40%).

Installed base as of March 31, 2025 of over 2,300 tape extrusion lines, over 468,000 winders and 96,000 circular weaving looms, with spare parts contributing 12.62% of FY2025 revenue from operations (FY2024 11.95%, FY2023 8.19%).

In-house R&D of 234 on-roll employees (13.48% of on-roll manpower as at May 31, 2025) and spend of ₹371.13 million (2.70% of FY2025 revenue); 60 patents granted in India, 56 granted globally, 8 registered designs, 53 registered trademarks.

Backward integration into inverters, customised machine controllers and motors, an in-house surface-mount-technology PCB assembly line, sheet-metal fabrication, 100 CNC machines and in-house plating, moulding, assembly, testing and paint shops.
Permanent-employee attrition improved to 11.39% in FY2025 from 22.83% in FY2024 (12.94% in FY2023); 1,736 permanent employees as of May 31, 2025.
